item.title: Autonomous Vehicle Perception System
item.description:
Overview

Autonomous Vehicle Perception is a group project developed for the Master MIATE Computer Vision course. It combines nine perception scenarios in one Tkinter application that can process video files, images, or a live camera depending on the selected scenario.

The repository describes the result as a final integrated university prototype. I served as the team leader and repository maintainer, coordinating the shared repository structure and integration while the scenarios were developed collaboratively by the team. This article focuses on the final main branch and does not claim that I personally implemented every detector.

item.title: LocalMind AI: A Local Multimodal AI Assistant
item.description:
Overview

LocalMind AI is a local-first multimodal AI assistant developed as an academic project with a teammate under the supervision of Anas Charroud. The application brings text interaction, image analysis, and audio input together in a browser-based interface.

The project explores how a web application can connect users to locally hosted AI models without relying on a remote model API for the core inference workflow. A FastAPI backend serves the interface and coordinates requests, Ollama runs the local vision-language model, and Whisper handles audio transcription.

item.title: Computer Vision Labs: OCR, Object Detection, Segmentation and Generative AI
item.description:
Overview

Computer Vision Labs is a collection of three practical experiments in computer vision and generative AI. The project combines image preprocessing, pretrained vision models, and diffusion-based generation to solve different tasks with separate workflows.

The labs cover:

  1. OCR with image preprocessing
  2. Object detection, segmentation, and relative depth estimation
  3. AI-powered interior redesign

1. OCR and Image Preprocessing

The first lab uses OpenCV and Tesseract OCR to extract text from a noisy image. The workflow improves the input before OCR rather than sending the raw image directly to Tesseract.

item.title: CampusVoice
item.description:
Overview

CampusVoice is a secure, anonymized feedback collection platform built for universities. It allows students to submit honest evaluations of courses and instructors without any login, while providing professors and administrators with actionable insights through a protected dashboard.

Built as a Cloud Computing mini-project for the Master’s program in AI & Emerging Technologies at FPN Nador.

Key Features

  • Anonymous Student Submissions — No login required, anonymity-first design
  • Role-Based Access Control — Separate interfaces for students, professors, and administrators
  • Real-time Dashboard — Filter, analyze, and export feedback data as CSV
  • Anti-Spam — One feedback per professor per day per IP, rate limiting (5 attempts / 60s)
  • Cloud-Native — Deployed on Microsoft Azure (PaaS architecture)

item.title: Ciora
item.description:
Overview

Ciora is a Bash-based recon automation tool built for bug bounty hunters and pentesters. It downloads the HackerOne program scope (public or private with session cookie), extracts web assets & wildcards, and optionally performs subdomain enumeration using multiple tools.

Features

  • Supports public & private HackerOne programs (cookie auth for private)
  • Automatically extracts:
    • Web assets
    • Wildcards
    • Cleaned wildcard domains
  • Subdomain enumeration with:
    • Amass
    • Sublist3r
    • Assetfinder
    • Subfinder
    • ShuffleDNS
  • Merges results into one file (all_subdomains.txt)
  • Pretty banner + clean output

item.title: E-commerce Customer Segmentation — Big Data & Machine Learning
item.description:
Overview

This project applies Big Data processing and machine learning to e-commerce transaction data. It builds customer-level features with RFM analysis, compares clustering approaches, and demonstrates how incoming transactions can be associated with previously computed customer segments.

The implementation uses Apache Spark and PySpark for distributed processing, Spark MLlib for K-Means clustering, and Kafka with Spark Structured Streaming for transaction enrichment.
